basis: Non-syndromic congenital fusion and duplication of digits affect the skeleton.
Umbrella of mitochondrial transport metabolic disorders; no additional organ damage is established as common across the group.
Defined by non-syndromic intellectual disability; the carbohydrate-transport ancestry does not establish a metabolic disorder across this umbrella.
Epilepsy and learning disability define the disorder; both are reported in 80-99%.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction and lissencephaly define the disease; respiratory infections 6/6 and lissencephaly 7/7. Otitis frequency is unspecified.
Biotin-dependent metabolic defect; seizures, perioral eczema and keratoconjunctivitis each occur in 80-99%. Tachypnea reflects acidosis rather than lung damage.
Predominantly an ovarian benign epithelial-stromal neoplasm, supported by the ovarian child concept; reproductive organs have no axis.
Neurodevelopmental and ocular disorder; patellar dislocation and nail dysplasia each 80-99%. Renal anomalies 5-29%; dysphagia alone does not establish gut damage.
Clonal marrow mast-cell neoplasm; cutaneous mast-cell lesions occur in >30%. Visceral enlargement without organ dysfunction does not establish hepatic damage.
Familial abdominal aortic aneurysm directly affects the aortic wall.
JPH2-related hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; myocardial hypertrophy and fibrosis affect the heart. Dyspnea does not establish lung damage.
Primary respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis; recurrent middle-ear disease is characteristic and affects >30% in PCD, though subtype frequency is unspecified.
Defined as disease of the cardiovascular system; additional organs are not shared across this broad umbrella.
Postsynaptic myasthenic syndrome with SCN4A-related skeletal-muscle dysfunction and periodic paralysis. Ophthalmoplegia and apnea reflect neuromuscular weakness.
Defined as a cutaneous smooth-muscle neoplasm of the dartos; its genital location does not remove its skin origin.
Abnormal kidney development directly affects renal structure and function. Hypertension and urinary infections are occasional complications.
Congenital enlargement of the cisterna magna is a posterior-fossa central nervous system malformation.
Acute inflammation and necrosis of exocrine pancreatic tissue; inflammation alone does not establish an autoimmune mechanism.
Ichthyosis, atrichia and ocular disease define IFAP; ectrodactyly occurs in 4/13 (~31%). Neurologic, renal and intestinal BRESHECK abnormalities are minority findings.
Neoplasm originating in an eccrine sweat gland, a skin appendage.
Tumour of the uterine corpus; reproductive organs are outside the 13 axes.
Structural outpouching of the urinary bladder; the renal axis includes the bladder.
Anterior-segment dysgenesis affecting the iris and iridocorneal angle; systemic features are not shared across the umbrella.
Inherited marrow failure; thumb/radial malformations occur in roughly 30-50% (absent thumb 2/4). Pigmentary spots are non-damaging; isolated cardiac reports do not establish frequency.
Infection causing inflammation throughout the uveal tract directly affects the eye and establishes the infectious mechanism.
